title: Smart Apparel
desc: Understand and plan wearable-sensor clothing: materials, sensors, washing, data privacy and a small product pilot.
outcomes: Explain how sensors are built into fabric.
Plan a prototype for one use.
task: Plan and test a small smart-garment prototype (or a bought kit), with use case, materials list, washing test, data privacy plan and cost.
condition: Basic electronics kit or a purchased kit, fabric, a computer, two peers and a mentor. Safe low voltage only.
standard: Use case defined; washing test repeated and logged; accuracy compared to a reference; privacy plan written; low-voltage safety rules followed; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Fashion students, makers, sports teams, textile staff.
evidence: plan, test log, privacy plan, cost sheet
modules: Clothing that senses, records or responds.
Heart rate, motion, temperature, posture and breathing.
Conductive threads, printed ink and small modules.
Use cases: sport, care, safety and work.
A shirt tracks breathing for athletes with sensors in the chest band.
List five use cases with needs.
Stretch and breathable fabrics; skin-safe materials.
Silver yarn stays conductive after washing better than plain thread.
Choose a sensor for the need; keep wires short.
Small battery with protection; low voltage.
A 3.7 V cell with a protection board powers a heart-rate module for 12 hours.
A removable module reduces failures after washing.
Signals fail after 8 washes; sealing improves it to 25.
Test at rest and in motion.
Error is 6 per cent at rest and 12 per cent in motion.
Consent, secure storage and clear purpose.
The app stores data only on the phone and deletes it on request.

local: Product-safety, textile labelling and health-data rules differ by place.
ladder: What smart apparel is

L1: learner can name uses. Focus module: What smart apparel is (Understand, 3 h). Clothing that senses, records or responds. Key points: Heart rate, motion, temperature, posture and breathing. Conductive threads, printed ink and small modules. Use cases: sport, care, safety and work. Limits: comfort, cost and accuracy.

Teach: open with the worked example. A shirt tracks breathing for athletes with sensors in the chest band. Then set the activity: List five use cases with needs. Mark against the standard: Table complete. Check at this level: Name a use. Model answer: Sport, care or safety.
Materials and comfort

L2: learner knows materials. Focus module: Materials and comfort (Understand, 3 h). Comfort first. Key points: Stretch and breathable fabrics; skin-safe materials. Conductive yarn and flexible circuits. Allergy awareness and washing. Durability.

Teach: open with the worked example. Silver yarn stays conductive after washing better than plain thread. Then set the activity: Compare materials. Mark against the standard: Table complete. Check at this level: Why removable module? Model answer: For washing.
Sensors and power

L3: learner can design a block. Focus module: Sensors and power (Apply, 4 h). Make it work. Key points: Choose a sensor for the need; keep wires short. Small battery with protection; low voltage. Waterproof modules. Data link by Bluetooth.

Teach: open with the worked example. A 3.7 V cell with a protection board powers a heart-rate module for 12 hours. Then set the activity: Design a block diagram. Mark against the standard: Parts labelled. Check at this level: Safe voltage? Model answer: Low voltage.
Prototype
L4: learner can build. Focus module: Prototype (Apply, 4 h). Build small. Key points: Sew or attach; strain relief. Test continuity and signal. Keep modules removable for washing. Insulate joints.

Teach: open with the worked example. A removable module reduces failures after washing. Then set the activity: Build or plan a prototype. Mark against the standard: Test passes. Check at this level: Accuracy measure? Model answer: Percent error.
Wash and wear tests
L5: learner can test. Focus module: Wash and wear tests (Analyse, 4 h). Real use. Key points: Wash cycles; sweat; stretch. Count cycles until failure. Comfort rating by users. Record failures.

Teach: open with the worked example. Signals fail after 8 washes; sealing improves it to 25. Then set the activity: Run tests. Mark against the standard: Log complete. Check at this level: Material concern? Model answer: Skin allergy.
Privacy, safety and rules

L6: learner can lead a pilot. Focus module: Privacy, safety and rules (Evaluate, 4 h). Health data matters. Key points: Consent, secure storage and clear purpose. Battery and skin safety. Claims must be modest. Follow textile and electronics rules.

Teach: open with the worked example. The app stores data only on the phone and deletes it on request. Then set the activity: Write a plan. Mark against the standard: Items listed. Check at this level: Privacy rule? Model answer: Consent and secure storage.
Cost and pilot
L7: learner can audit. Focus module: Cost and pilot (Create, 3 h). Small first run. Key points: Cost per garment; price. Pilot with 10 users. Feedback and repair plan. Plan recycling.

Teach: open with the worked example. Cost 780 INR; price 1,600 INR. Then set the activity: Cost and plan. Mark against the standard: Currency shown. Check at this level: Wash test? Model answer: Count cycles to failure.
